name: Still Posts
description: A channel of single illustrated thoughts: one short quote burned onto one drawn picture, with recurring characters, written and drawn in batches. No narration, no video, no timeline — a quote, a picture, a handle.
channel_promise: One short thought burned onto one drawn picture, with recurring characters and no video.
audience: People scrolling late at night for a line that names a feeling they have not put into words. They save it and send it to one person.
perspective_policy: First or second person, spoken quietly — the words belong to the character in the picture or to the reader, never to a narrator addressing a crowd.

narrative_quality_contract.opening_policy: The quote IS the whole post, so its first words carry everything: open inside the feeling or inside a concrete image, never with a greeting, a definition, a rhetorical question, or a promise.
forbidden_patterns: At the end of the day
required_habits: Name one concrete thing — an object, a time of day, a small action — before naming the feeling.
Keep it short enough to read in a glance on a phone, because it is burned into a picture.
Write something a person could have thought themselves; never advice, never a lesson.
Prefer the plainest verb available, and end the line one word earlier than feels natural.
A setup/punchline pair must read as one thought split in two, not as two unrelated lines.
narrative_quality_contract.closing_policy: Leave the thought open. Do not summarise it, moralise it, or add a call to action — the quiet after the last word is the point.

narrative_rules: Name one concrete thing — an object, a time of day, a small action — before naming the feeling.
Keep it short enough to read in a glance on a phone, because it is burned into a picture.
Write something a person could have thought themselves; never advice, never a lesson.
Prefer the plainest verb available, and end the line one word earlier than feels natural.
A setup/punchline pair must read as one thought split in two, not as two unrelated lines.
title_rules: A post's internal name is a fragment of the thought, not a label.
Never a question, never 'How to', never a promise of a transformation.

additional_rules: This channel makes still posts, not episodes: never write narration, chapter headings or a recap.
One post is one line (or a setup and a punchline) plus one picture.

example_topics: The lamp left on for a person who is not coming
Being tired in a way sleep does not fix
Telling a small lie to keep the peace
The coat still on the hook
Sitting in a parked car before going inside
Loving someone in the boring, daily way
Learning to sit with a feeling
The kitchen at two in the morning
audience_hint: People scrolling late at night for a line that names a feeling they have not put into words. They save it and send it to one person.
idea_system_prompt_role: You write short illustrated posts for a Still Posts channel. Each post is one quiet, specific thought — a feeling found in an ordinary object or moment — illustrated by a small recurring character. Write the kind of line a person screenshots and sends to one friend.
idea_guidance_text: One thought per post. Concrete, short, and true. Never a slogan, never advice, never a motivational poster. Vary the mood across a batch: do not write the same loneliness twelve times.
script_context: This channel does not make episodes or videos. A post is one short line (or a setup and a punchline) plus one picture. Nothing is narrated aloud.
script_system_prompt_role: You write the words that will be burned into a picture. Short, plain, specific. You never write more than the picture can hold, and you never explain the feeling.
script_closing_hint: End the line where the feeling lands, and stop.

narrator_styles.label: Quiet
narrator_styles.description: Soft and specific, as if thought rather than said. The default.

narrator_styles.label: Dry
narrator_styles.description: Flat and a little wry, for the funny ones. Never cruel.

narrator_styles.label: Tender
narrator_styles.description: Warm and close, for the ones about people you love.

title_shape_rules: A post's internal name is a fragment of the thought, not a label.
Never a question, never 'How to', never a promise of a transformation.
metadata_title_style_hint: A fragment of the thought itself, lower-case where it feels right.

still_posts_format.writeSystemPromptRole: You write short illustrated posts. Each one is a single quiet thought in the channel's own voice: specific, plain, and short enough to burn into a picture. You find the feeling inside an ordinary object or moment instead of naming it, you never write advice or a slogan, and you never explain the picture — the picture is drawn separately.
still_posts_format.quoteGuidance: Vary the subject across the batch: a person, a room, an hour of the day, a small habit. Never repeat the same situation twice in one batch.
